statutes.act: Read With Section 34 Of The Indian Penal Code

facts: The appellant was a student of B.A. Part II of D.B.S. (P.G.) College.

On January 31, 2000, when Surendra Kumar Sehgal was entering the college through its gate to attend his N.C.C. class, the appellant along with three other persons who were armed with 'Khukries' assaulted him on instigation made by the appellant as a result whereof he suffered five injuries.
The FIR was lodged on the same day at about 3:15 p.m.
The first informant, Surendra Kumar Sehgal, examined himself as P.W.2 and stated that the incident occurred at about 1:00 p.m. on January 31, 2000.
issues: Whether the appellant was armed with a 'Khukri' during the assault
Whether the prosecution has proved that the appellant instigated the other accused to commit the offence
petitioner_arguments: The FIR does not disclose that the appellant was armed with a 'Khukri'
The improvement in the depositions of the complainant before the court is an outcome of which the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside
Out of four accused, three having been acquitted, the appellant could not have been convicted with the aid of Section 34 of the IPC
respondent_arguments: The FIR categorically states that the appellant along with three others who were armed with 'Khukri' accosted Surendra Kumar Sehgal at about 1:00 p.m. on January 31, 2000
The prosecution has proved that the appellant instigated the other accused to commit the offence
court_reasoning: Although the FIR is not an encyclopedia, it would not be proper to accept that all particulars in regard to commission of offence in detail must be furnished
The testimony of Surendra (P.W.2) - informant - had been relied upon by both the courts below
We do not think that any case has been made out to take a different view
